sections.heading: 1. Force
points: A **force** is a **push or a pull** on an object.
Force arises from an **interaction** between objects; measured in **newtons (N)**.

points.text: Effects of force — a force can:
sub: Move a stationary object, or stop a moving one.
**Friction** — opposes motion between surfaces in contact.
**Gravitational force** — the pull of the Earth (and all masses); makes things fall.

sections.heading: 3. Pressure
points: **Pressure = Force ÷ Area** (force acting on a unit area).
**Smaller area → greater pressure** (sharp knives, nails have pointed ends); **larger area → less pressure** (wide straps, camel's broad feet, foundations of buildings).

sections.heading: 4. Pressure of Liquids, Gases and Air
points: **Liquids and gases exert pressure** on the walls of their container and **increase with depth**.
**Atmospheric pressure** = the pressure exerted by the **weight of air** around us; it is very large but we don't feel it because the pressure inside our body balances it.
A **suction cup**, drinking through a straw, and a **barometer** work due to atmospheric pressure.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Force = push or pull (unit: newton); can change speed, direction or shape.
Contact forces: muscular, friction; non-contact: magnetic, electrostatic, gravitational.
Pressure = Force ÷ Area (unit: pascal); smaller area → more pressure.
Liquids/gases exert pressure; it increases with depth.
Atmospheric pressure = weight of air; balanced by pressure inside our body.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Pressure = Force ÷ Area** — for the same force, a **smaller area gives more pressure** (sharp knife).
**Gravity, magnetic and electrostatic forces are non-contact** forces.
We don't feel atmospheric pressure because our **internal pressure balances** it.
